analyzed_vuln.description: The root cause is an unsafe internal invariant enforced with `assert(dat->byte == 0xb)` at the start of `decode_R13_R2000` instead of validating attacker-controlled parsing state and returning an error. A crafted AC1015 (R13-R2000 path) input can reach this function with `dat->byte` not equal to 0xb, causing immediate abort via assertion (DoS) rather than graceful `DWG_ERR_INVALIDDWG` handling.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Via `llvmfuzz` harness, any input beginning with `AC` is passed to `dwg_decode`. If magic selects R13-R2000 decoding (e.g., AC1015) and the malformed header/bitstream causes parser position `dat->byte` to differ from expected 0xb before header.spec parsing, `decode_R13_R2000` hits the assert and aborts. The PoC is a short malformed DWG-like blob that satisfies version dispatch but violates this byte-offset assumption.
